subject: Scope inventory + remediation triage for upcoming penetration test
messages:
From: Wayne Harris <wayne.harris@stellardata.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Request: pen test scope & report access for renewal

Hi Kimberly,

Hope you and the team are well. As part of our annual security renewal we need:

- A copy of Redwood's most recent external penetration test report (or redacted findings) covering services we use.
- Clear confirmation of which deployment variants are covered: Hosted API (multi-tenant), Dedicated (reserved pools), Private/VPC, and on-prem (if any).
- A short asset mapping for our account (hostnames, endpoints) so our internal assessor can align findings.

We currently integrate with your Hosted API and have a Dedicated instance. Our assessor flagged uncertainty about whether Dedicated customer pools are in-scope for your hosted PT or treated as separate. Can you confirm? Also send any authorization or NDA forms you require to share redacted reports.

Thanks — we need this by end of week to keep our procurement timeline on track.

Regards,
Wayne Harris
Head of Infrastructure Security
StellarData

Attachments: none

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Wayne Harris <wayne.harris@stellardata.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 14:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: pen test scope & report access for renewal

Hi Wayne — thanks for the clear ask. Quick answers up top:

- We can provide a redacted external pen test report and a scope matrix.
- Hosted (our multi-tenant public API) and Redwood-managed Dedicated pools are covered by our standard external engagements.
- Private/VPC deployments and on-prem packages are NOT automatically in scope unless the customer is on our managed Private plan and opts into the engagement; for air-gapped on-prem customers we require a bespoke engagement.

I've attached: redwood-scope-matrix-2026-08.csv (maps component -> hosting variant) and pt-authorization-form-Redwood.pdf (standard form we ask customers to sign to receive redacted findings). Also attaching a remediation-triage-sheet.xlsx template so we can align owners and timelines.

A few clarifying notes (technical):
- "Dedicated" here means Redwood-managed reserved GPU pools tied to your account (we run the hosts, we manage the hypervisor and base OS). Those are included in our external tests.
- "Private/VPC" (Redwood Private in a customer VPC) is covered only if the engagement includes our managed nodes; if your Dedicated instance was provisioned as an isolated, customer-managed VM group inside your VPC, that falls under Private and requires a scoped engagement.

Next steps I propose:
1) You review the attached scope matrix and mark any assets you believe are customer-owned/unmanaged.
2) Sign and return the authorization form so we can share the redacted report.
3) Vanessa (cc) will coordinate a short inventory call tomorrow with your assessor to reconcile hostnames and endpoints.

If that works, we can target shared materials by Thursday.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Manager, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 16:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: pen test scope & report access for renewal

Wayne — quick technical clarifications from our side to avoid ambiguity on the call:

- In-scope (standard engagement):
  * Public Hosted API endpoints (api.redwood.ai) and associated frontend edge services.
  * Redwood-managed Dedicated pools (customer-allocated but infra-managed by Redwood; includes host OS and hypervisor).
  * Central control plane components (RBAC, billing APIs) that are common to Hosted + Dedicated.

- Out-of-scope unless explicitly included:
  * Customer-managed VPC endpoints and on-prem appliances (we do not test inside customer-managed networks unless a scoped, customer-authorized engagement is arranged).
  * Third-party partner-managed integrations unless the contract includes Redwood responsibility.

On remediation triage: we ask that you assign an internal StellarData owner for each asset you mark as customer-managed so we can split the remediation matrix between Redwood and StellarData rows. We've added a sample owner column in remediation-triage-sheet.xlsx.

I'll be on the inventory call and can answer technical asset questions (hostnames, control-plane endpoints to exclude, etc.).

-Aditya
Lead Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks — a couple of follow-ups from our assessor:

1) We have a Dedicated instance that was provisioned in January 2026. The deployment is "managed by Redwood" but the VPC/subnet is in our cloud account; we manage IAM and some network ACLs. Does that change the inclusion?

2) For items you list as "control plane components" can you provide a short list of specific endpoints and the expected contact points we should exclude from our inventory? Our assessor specifically asked for the API hostnames used for billing and RBAC so they don't attempt authenticated fuzzing without coordination.

3) Are there any known findings from the last engagement that we should expect to see as redactions (e.g., low-severity infra findings) so we can plan for remediation expectations?

We can do the inventory call tomorrow 09:00 PT if that works.

Subject: Re: Request: pen test scope & report access for renewal

Samira — thanks for the precise questions. Quick answers and next steps below.

1) Dedicated provisioned in your cloud account but "managed by Redwood" — included in our standard engagement. The determining factor is whether Redwood operates the compute and orchestration layer. If we perform OS/hypervisor patching and have access, it's in-scope. If you retained full control and we only have API access, it becomes Private/VPC. Based on what you described (we manage the instance) it's in-scope. Please mark this in the scope matrix as "Redwood-managed (in-scope)".

2) Control plane endpoints (examples to exclude from autonomous scanning unless coordinated):
   - control.redwood.ai (RBAC, user management)
   - billing-api.redwood.ai
   - internal-metrics.redwood.ai (read-only telemetry endpoints)

We will provide a short allowlist of hostnames and IP ranges prior to any active testing. Aditya will post the allowlist to the shared JIRA ticket (RED-4521) and to the DocuSign access request once the authorization form is returned.

3) Redactions: we redact customer-identifying details and any low-risk internal hostnames. The report will include severity buckets and generalized remediation notes. There were no critical/high findings in the last 2025 external engagement — you should expect a handful of low/medium infra observations that we will redact specific hostnames for.

Remediation & owners:
- Redwood-owned items: assigned to Aditya Rao (lead) — ETA initial remediation plan 2 weeks after report delivery.
- StellarData-owned items: please populate the "owner" column in remediation-triage-sheet.xlsx; Kimberly will coordinate weekly syncs until closure.

Inventory call confirmed: Tomorrow 09:00 PT (calendar invite to follow from Vanessa). Once we have the signed authorization form we will upload the redacted report to the DocuSign link and attach the allowlist.

Thanks — aiming to keep your procurement timeline intact.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Manager, Customer Security
Redwood Inference
